name: Build 10
body:
feat: rounded font, green in-tune feedback, instrument picker

The font was the right family with the wrong axis. Google Sans Flex carries a
ROND axis and the default instances are ROND=0, which is why it had none of
the roundness it is recognised for. All three weights are re-fetched at
ROND=100.

The chime was inaudible for a reason that had nothing to do with detection: it
published on USAGE_ASSISTANCE_SONIFICATION, which routes to the system stream,
and that sits at zero on any phone kept on silent. It plays as media now, the
stream someone tuning a guitar has audible by definition. SoundPool.load is
also asynchronous, so the load result is tracked rather than letting an early
play be a silent no-op.

In tune is now green, everywhere, and live. The original spec put the scheme's
primary at the centre of the meter, which says nothing: on a blue wallpaper it
lands next to the sharp accent, so the one state the user is hunting for looks
like the state beside it. The active peg also turns green the moment the note
lands rather than half a second later when the hold completes, driven by a
Boolean StateFlow through distinctUntilChanged so the headstock recomposes a
couple of times per string instead of a couple of hundred.

The chip row is gone. Six instruments never fit, so one was always sliced off
at the fade edge, and a row of competing pills above the meter was noise
around the thing being read. One button states the instrument and opens a
sheet. Each option carries a miniature of the headstock it actually gets,
drawn from the same peg layout the full component uses: literal instrument
pictures would have been clip art, and six guitar silhouettes at 26dp are
indistinguishable from each other anyway.

Icon: matching the compass's stroke ratio exactly still read as heavier,
because matching stroke width does not match perceived weight when one mark is
a wide thin ring and the other packs its ink into a solid head. This version
is more linear instead: 6.2 stroke, a slanted ellipse head at real notation
proportions, longer stem.
